title: Asking for honesty while needing one reply

captions.physics: Invoking a recognised value of sincerity
captions.emotions: Clinging to the response you want

meaning: Shared words about sincerity help you speak openly, even while an honest answer different from the one desired can be emotionally difficult to accept.
text: A request for sincerity does not always coincide with readiness to hear any answer. The Hierophant in the physical position of Vishuddha invokes the recognised value of honest speech and familiar formulas of trust. The Sun in energy supports openness: speaking directly without concealing essentials in hints. The Devil in emotions shows a grip on a desired reaction. You can genuinely want clarity while strongly hoping for praise or agreement. Naming that expectation separately keeps it distinct from any supposed promise by the other person to give the needed reply.

For example, you ask, “Honestly, what do you think of my letter?” A specific correction comes back when approval was what you most wanted. **An open request leaves an honest answer free.** You can acknowledge a wish for support and discuss the remark separately. A familiar formula of sincerity leaves the listener free from guessing which truth is permitted. The letter and the need for warm participation become two clear subjects.

The difficulty is refining the question until the desired response appears. Outwardly the letter is discussed; inwardly the exchange increasingly depends on confirmation of personal importance. Asking directly for encouragement preserves honest words. Support can stand beside disagreement, remaining kind and freely given without cancelling an actual observation.
